sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU by default and WebGL 2 compatibility fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.28.2 build tool. All runtime dependencies, WASM and fonts embedded.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded 3D, navy ink outlines, cream ice, teal and coral uniforms, yellow sports graphics
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip: skating, stick swing, body check and celebration; procedural puck trails, ice spray and confetti
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written chiptune rink music (10% default), synthesized hits, skates, crowd, horns and Animalese-style formant gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world online 1–4 players, authoritative host, input counters and world snapshots; standalone couch multiplayer 1–4 players
sourceInformation.testing: Headless testing as authorized: deterministic Rapier checks and full AI match, Chromium 153 WebGPU, emulated standard gamepads for 1–4 seats, two keyboards, Pixel 7 touch gestures, Web Audio analyser, file:// boot, four official AI Hub scenarios including 150 ms latency / 50 ms jitter / 5% loss. Visual screenshots use WebGL compatibility because software WebGPU capture is unreliable. Physical controller, real mobile hardware and subjective listening quality: unknown. Full automated regression: 143/143 checks passed; isolated package/visual pass: 48/48.
sourceInformation.research: none; no internet search or source research. Downloaded only dependencies and the explicitly requested AI Hub contract, client and harness.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 4 confirmed game/package issues caught: scoreless AI, occluded rink advertising, foreground light rigs obstructing the rink, and HTML template substitution corrupting minified JavaScript. All corrected. Test-only selector and timing errors were corrected separately.

1 critical issue: a late package build produced a JavaScript syntax error. Literal insertion and a package-integrity guard fixed it before delivery. Physical controller feel, real phone behavior and subjective sound quality are unknown.
The deterministic full AI match exposed scoreless AI play. The official AI Hub harness also verified normal two-player play, stressed four-player play, host departure and dedicated-server hosting.

Raw pixel capture from headless software WebGPU was least helpful: frames could be blank and readback failed. Gameplay was checked from state, while isolated WebGL compatibility screenshots verified appearance.
engineFeedback: Three.js node materials and AnimationMixer made it possible to build an entirely procedural ink-styled rink with animated skaters and no asset downloads at runtime.

Software WebGPU screenshots/readback were unreliable. A late build also exposed JavaScript replacement-string interpretation of minified code; the builder now inserts code literally and rejects unresolved template slots. Visual capture is isolated from input tests.
The hockey simulation: possession, team AI, checking, passing, goalies, match flow, input routing and the authoritative shared-world network layer.
Coordinating fixed-step Rapier physics, Three.js animation, WebGPU presentation, controller focus and delayed network input without losing brief button actions.
none; the engines and AI Hub client are unmodified. Custom materials, gameplay and compatibility options are application code.
A first-class cel-shading material for WebGPU with straightforward ink outlines would reduce custom material work.
promptFeedback: The specific source, procedural audio, cel/ink art direction and controller-first constraints gave the demo a clear identity while leaving room for original arcade mechanics.

The terse source label and whether standalone multiplayer required internet play outside AI Hub were ambiguous. This demo provides standalone couch multiplayer and online shared-world play through AI Hub.
Making a complete hockey match, six-drill tutorial, multi-device controls, dev tools and resilient multiplayer fit together in one self-contained HTML.
Provide the Hub contract locally and specify whether standalone multiplayer must include internet play in addition to couch play.

aiHub.name: Puck Wild
aiHub.description: A punchy arcade hockey game with chunky skaters, bank passes, charged slapshots and no penalties. Take the Wild Cup solo, battle on the couch, or share a rink with up to four players in AI Hub.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick skate; Space / R2 hold & release shoot; E / Cross pass; Q / Square check; Shift / R1 burst; Tab / L1 switch; Esc / Options menu. Touch drag to skate, hold/release to shoot.
